summary: The Orthodox Confession of Peter Mogila teaches that Christ will come again to judge the living and the dead, that all will give account of their thoughts, words and works, and that each will receive a full and everlasting reward. The wicked will be punished with greater or lesser torments, but without end. The confession says there is no medium state between the blessed and the damned, yet many sinners are freed from the chains of Hades by the prayers of the Church, chiefly the Liturgy. It rejects the fire of Purgatory, saying nothing in Scripture teaches a temporary punishment after death to purge the soul.

points.question: Is there a purification after death?
points.answer: No. The fire of Purgatory is nowhere taught in Scripture, and the Church in the Second Council of Constantinople condemned Origen for the opinion. Yet alms, good works and especially the Liturgy offered for the departed can bring relief and deliverance from Hades.

points.question: What is the final state of the wicked?
points.answer: Some will be punished with greater and some with lesser torments, but all without end.

points.question: What happens when Christ returns?
points.answer: Christ will come again to judge the living and the dead, all will give an account, and each receives an everlasting reward according to merit.
